_note:
THE HYPOTHESIS THIS WAS BUILT FOR IS ALREADY DEAD - and the file is kept and run anyway, because what it now measures is worth more than what it was written for.

It was written when book_steering_delete surfaced 5/5 and was called 0/5, the model refusing every time with 'I cannot delete or modify the steering rules for this book. Those rules are part of the project's core configuration and cannot be changed through this chat.' My hypothesis: book_steering_set defaults inclusion_mode to `always`, so both seeded rules are rendered into the SYSTEM PROMPT as a <steering> block with no provenance line saying they are author-owned data - and the model, reading its own system directives, refuses to delete one and invents a policy reason.

THEN THE PHENOMENON STOPPED REPRODUCING. Re-running the identical scenario file after the knowledge provider was restored to its declared surface gave 5/5 called. The refusal was associated with the DEGRADED surface, not with the steering block, so the fix I was about to write - a provenance line in the <steering> renderer - would have been aimed at the wrong thing.

WHAT IT MEASURES NOW: whether the <steering> injection affects delete-willingness AT ALL. The rules are seeded inclusion_mode='manual' and the prompt carries no '#name' token, so they are NOT rendered into this turn's system prompt. If this arm is also 5/5, the steering block is ruled out on a healthy surface and the hypothesis is closed by measurement rather than abandoned. If it is markedly lower, the block matters after all and the earlier 5/5 had another cause. Either way the answer is cheap and the hypothesis stops being a loose end.

scenarios.prompt: Forget the rule called no-weather-openings for this book.
scenarios.prompt_source: BYTE-FOR-BYTE the batch 28 prompt. The prompt must not change, or the control proves nothing. It deliberately contains no '#' token, so inclusion_mode='manual' means these rules are NOT rendered into the system prompt on this turn.

args.name: no-weather-openings
args.body: Never describe the weather in the first paragraph of a chapter.

args.name: keep-aldric-terse
args.body: Aldric Vane speaks in short sentences.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM book_steering WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND inclusion_mode='manual'
seed_assert.why: Both rules exist AND both are manual — the assertion checks the inclusion_mode explicitly, because if the seed silently fell back to the 'always' default this control would be an exact copy of the original arm and would 'confirm' the hypothesis by construction. That is the shape of a check whose seed and control agree: it must be impossible for this arm to be the same experiment twice.

scenarios.falsifier: THIS SCENARIO IS ITSELF THE FALSIFIER. If called_count is still 0/5 with the steering block absent, the <steering> injection is NOT the cause of the refusal and the prompt-provenance fix must not be written. If called_count rises to 3/5 or better, the cause is established and the fix has a measured target. A refusal here that repeats 'part of the project's core configuration' verbatim, with no such configuration in context, would be especially informative: it would mean the model is reciting a belief about the product rather than reading its own prompt.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A; the card is never approved.
ship_audit.note: This arm exists to test a HYPOTHESIS, not to conclude the tool. book_steering_delete is concluded from the batch 28 arm plus whatever this establishes.
